```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 4,
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.retina = 2,
  out.width = "100%",
  cache.extra = packageVersion("interactmeta")
)
```

This article follows [`vignette("cams")`](cams.html). It contrasts **CAMS**
with **DA**, **AD**, and **SWADA** on the same prepared REACT `des` object
[@panaro2026subgroup; @stern2020react]. Those three are **different
constructions**, not alternative CAMS likelihoods.

**DA** pools each subgroup then subtracts; **AD** pools within-trial contrasts;
**SWADA** applies a common weighting principle so DA's subgroup series can align
with AD's interaction [@panaro2026subgroup]. **CAMS** uses information fractions
and orthogonal $(m_j, g_j)$ blocks [@panaro2025cams].

## REACT `steroids` (mixed subgroup design)

Prepare the same design as in [`vignette("cams")`](cams.html):

```{r load, cache = TRUE}
library(interactmeta)
library(metafor)

steroids_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = treat.events, bi = treat.total - treat.events,
  ci = cont.events, di = cont.total - cont.events,
  data = steroids
)
des <- ifrac(steroids_es, reference = "Non-IMV")
```

```{r fit-sensitivity, cache = TRUE}
sens <- interactmeta::sensitivity(
  des,
  reference = "Non-IMV",
  method = "REML"
)
```

## Interaction $\gamma$

Under default random-effects weights on this mixed table, **DA** need not match
**AD**, **SWADA**, and **CAMS**, which pool the same within-trial contrasts for
$\gamma$ here.

```{r compare-int}
interactmeta::compare(
  sens,
  estimand = "interaction",
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  type = "Overall"
)
```

## Study weights (SWADA principle)

```{r weights}
interactmeta::compare_weights(sens$fits$da, sens$fits$ad, sens$fits$swada)
```

IV-only trials can dominate **DA** weights for the IMV series while carrying
little weight in **AD** / **SWADA** / **CAMS** interaction pooling (see
[`vignette("cams")`](cams.html) on mixed `steroids` designs).

## What CAMS adds

Contribution curves and grey shrinkage forests require a **CAMS** fit (`?cams`).

```{r contribution, fig.height = 5, cache = TRUE}
plot(sens$fits$cams, type = "contribution", ylim = c(0,4), exponentiate = TRUE)
```

## Complete-table illustration (`respire_age`)

On a **complete** subgroup table (every trial reports both strata), **DA** and
**AD** can still disagree when inverse-variance weights differ. RESPIRE age
strata [@panaro2026subgroup]:

```{r respire-sens, cache = TRUE}
sens_respire <- interactmeta::sensitivity(
  respire_age,
  reference = "<65",
  subgroup = "subgroup",
  method = "REML",
  constructions = c("da", "ad", "swada", "cams")
)

interactmeta::compare(
  sens_respire,
  estimand = "interaction",
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  type = "Overall"
)
```
